If you’re implementing DeepL FR→DE, here’s a concise review checklist I’ll use (with GT‑C++17 Standard references):

- Secrets and config (GT‑C++17 §9.2): No hardcoded API keys; load via the approved secrets manager and pass via env/config. Ensure keys never appear in logs or tests.
- Error handling and retries (GT‑C++17 §3.2): Handle HTTP 4xx/5xx, timeouts, and network errors. Use bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter; fail fast on 401/403.
- Input validation (GT‑C++17 §9.5): Validate language codes, enforce UTF‑8, and sanitize user-provided text length/characters to avoid injection into headers/URLs.
- Internationalization/encoding (GT‑C++17 §10.1): Normalize to UTF‑8, handle surrogate pairs/emoji, and preserve punctuation/whitespace. Verify proper handling of HTML/Markdown if applicable.
- Performance and resource use (GT‑C++17 §6.3, §5.1): Reuse a single HTTP client with connection pooling/keep‑alive. Set sane timeouts. Avoid unnecessary copies; prefer string_views where safe. RAII for network resources.
- Concurrency/async (GT‑C++17 §4.2): Make the translator component thread-safe. Use async futures/tasks; don’t block UI or hot paths. Guard shared caches with appropriate synchronization.
- Rate limiting (GT‑C++17 §6.3): Implement client-side rate limiting and backoff on 429. Optional batching where supported.
- Logging/telemetry (GT‑C++17 §7.2): Log request IDs and status, not payloads or secrets. Redact sensitive fields. Include metrics for latency, error rates, retries.
- API boundaries (GT‑C++17 §2.1): Clear interfaces (e.g., ITranslator with translate(text, source, target)). Separate concerns: transport, auth, business logic.
- Testing and coverage (GT‑C++17 §8.1): ≥95% unit test coverage. Mock the HTTP/DeepL client; cover success, 4xx/5xx, timeouts, retries, rate limits, and encoding edge cases. Include property tests for round‑trip invariants if applicable. Provide an lcov/coverage.xml so I can verify the threshold.
- Feature flags/config (GT‑C++17 §9.2): Gate rollout with a flag; default safe behavior if config/secrets are missing. Ensure no flag values leak into logs.

To proceed, please provide:
- PR link or the unified diff
- Any new config files and CI changes
- Latest unit test report and coverage artifact (lcov or coverage.xml)

I’ll then give targeted comments and confirm the 95% coverage requirement. If I spot any uncertain security concerns, I’ll recommend escalating to Security Engineering.
